title: A small virtual machine
description:
Build a virtual machine with memory, registers and jumps, and run a program that adds up an array.

```
memory: 10 20 30 40
program: sum the 4 numbers with a loop
result in A: 100 (and how many instructions ran)
```
hints: The loop: B is the address, C the count; each time, `LOAD D B`, `ADD A D`, `ADDI B 1`, `DEC C`, `JNZ C loop` (lesson 1.04).
Print each instruction as it runs while you debug the program, then turn the printing off.
requirements: 4 registers, 256 cells of memory, and instructions `LOADI`, `LOAD` (from memory at a register), `ADD`, `ADDI`, `JNZ`, `DEC`, `HALT`.
Write the summing program as data in `main`.
Refuse memory addresses outside 0 to 255 with an error that names the instruction.
stretch: Add `CALL` and `RET` using a stack in memory.
